Working in /opt/nxeon-v2 (Next.js app, branch design/v2, a hosting platform's deploy wizard). This is a WRITE task based on real, hands-on bug reports from the site owner testing the live deploy wizard. Fix each one precisely, matching the existing codebase's style (terse comments explaining WHY, not WHAT).

All of these are in `components/nx/DeployView.tsx` unless noted. Read the relevant section fully before editing.

1. **Black text on a purple button is unreadable.** On the VPS plan-selection step, the "Selected" state of the chosen plan card renders a purple/gradient button with black (or otherwise low-contrast) text on it. Find this button (search for the plan card / "Selected" button markup, likely involving a `.card-on` or similar selected-state class) and fix the text color so it has real contrast against the purple background in BOTH light and dark mode — check app/globals.css for how `.card-on` or the equivalent selected-state class is styled, and whether a text-color rule needs adding/fixing there instead of inline.

2. **Can't see all OS versions.** The "Server settings → Operating system" grid (AlmaLinux, AlmaLinux, Debian, Rocky Linux, Ubuntu, etc.) gets cut off — the panel doesn't scroll or wrap to show every option, some are clipped off the visible edge. Find this OS-selection grid and fix it so all options are reachable — either wrap correctly, add horizontal/vertical scroll with a visible affordance, or resize the container to fit its content. Do not just guess; find the actual layout classes involved and diagnose why it's clipping (fixed height/width vs. content overflow).

3. **The Add-ons checkbox (e.g. "Backup Plus") doesn't read as clearly on/off.** Compare the styling of an unchecked checkbox item next to a checked one (e.g. "Dedicated IP" which shows selected). If the checked/unchecked visual states are too similar (low contrast on the check icon, or the selected border/background isn't distinct enough), strengthen the visual distinction — this is a real usability complaint, not just an aesthetic nitpick.

4. **The "Recommended" tag/badge styling is bad SITE-WIDE**, not just on this page — low contrast, hard to read. Search `app/globals.css` for the shared tag/badge class this uses (likely something used across multiple cards, search for a class like `.nx-tag` or similar rendering "Recommended" badges) and improve its contrast in both light and dark mode. Check everywhere it's used (grep for the class name) to make sure the fix helps across the site, not just one spot.

5. **Region selection on the deploy wizard's globe/region-picker only shows Singapore, but the platform also has a Germany location available.** Find where the region picker's list of selectable regions is built (likely reading from `lib/node-regions.ts` or a similar catalog/config file, and rendered in DeployView.tsx's region step) and figure out why Germany isn't appearing — check if a Germany node/region exists in the config but is filtered out (e.g. by an `active`/`enabled` flag, node capacity check, or the query only fetches nodes with a specific provider), or if Germany genuinely isn't configured as a region option at all yet. Report clearly which it is. If it's a simple filter/query bug (a real region exists but isn't surfaced), fix it. If Germany was never actually configured as an available region anywhere in the codebase (no node, no config entry), do NOT fabricate one — report this back clearly as something that needs a real node/region added by the owner, not a code bug you can fix.

6. **Cloud/Shared Hosting should show "first month free" promotional messaging** on the deploy wizard, matching a real site-wide promotion already visible elsewhere (the site owner mentioned "we have this promotion" — search the codebase for existing "first month free" messaging, e.g. `grep -rn "first month free" --include="*.tsx"` to find where this promo is ALREADY implemented/displayed elsewhere on the site, likely a marketing banner or the hosting plan cards) and confirm/add the same messaging to the Cloud Hosting service selection step of THIS wizard if it's missing there specifically.

After each fix, run `cd /opt/nxeon-v2 && npx tsc --noEmit` and resolve any type errors. Do not touch files outside `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, `app/globals.css`, `lib/node-regions.ts` unless you find the "first month free" messaging lives in a specific shared component worth reading (read-only) for reference. Do not commit — leave changes unstaged for review. Report back file-by-file with line numbers, and be explicit and honest about item 5 (Germany region) — say clearly whether you fixed a real bug or found a genuine missing-region gap that needs the owner's input.

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork **This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. This file is the operating manual; that one is the direction and the history of what has been built. --- ## Where you are, and what that changes This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else: ```bash hostname # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node. ``` **On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here: ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # always, before a build ./rebuild.sh # stop, build, restart. ~125s. ``` **On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst, terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A `next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must, then: ```bash scripts/deploy-node2.sh # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2 ``` It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory) and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't. **One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's commits. Schema changes: `npm run db:push`. There are no migration files. The primary node and node-2 have **separate** `nxeon_v2` databases, so a push on one does nothing to the other. ## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against. This supersedes the "treat it as read-only, ask first" rule that used to sit here — the routine build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask. Anything added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` must be added to `components/nx/Shell.tsx` too. ## Conventions inherited from the platform (still true here) - Every VM state change goes through a `Job` row. The web app never calls Proxmox mutation endpoints directly. - One in-flight job per server. - Wallet amounts are integer cents. - Admin-only actions call `requireAdmin()` and refuse to render while impersonating. - Charts are dependency-free SVG in `components/ui/charts.tsx`. Do not add a charting library. ## Inherited instructions that do NOT apply here The production `CLAUDE.md` this replaced is kept at `docs/CLAUDE-production-inherited.md` for reference. It describes the PRIMARY node. To avoid a very expensive mistake: - **Do not** run `systemctl restart nxeon-web nxeon-worker` — that is production. This tree's unit is `nxeon-v2-web`. - **Do not** publish docs to `revsports.ca/docs` from here. - ~~Do not run `scripts/promote-production.sh` or `scripts/deploy-staging.sh`~~ — **superseded 2026-09-12.** The owner authorized running these directly from this session; see the guardrails in "Reaching node-1" above. - There is no post-commit auto-push hook on node-2, and there should not be: `design/v2` is a design fork, not something to push to `origin` casually.

## Summary

**Files changed:** `components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, `app/globals.css`. `lib/node-regions.ts` was read but not touched (see item 5). Nothing committed — changes are unstaged for review. `npx tsc --noEmit` passes with no errors after every edit.

### 1. Black text on purple "Selected" button
Root cause: this button (and three siblings using the exact same recipe) use Tailwind's `text-white`, which in this app resolves through the `--color-white` token. Light theme deliberately flips that token to near-black ink (`app/globals.css:298`) for ordinary headings — correct for headings, wrong for text sitting on a hardcoded purple/blue gradient fill that never changes with the theme. The actual markup lives in `components/nx/OrderBits.tsx` (imported by `DeployView.tsx`), outside the files I was told to edit, so I fixed it at the CSS layer instead: added a light-mode override in `app/globals.css` (~line 424) that forces literal white wherever `bg-[linear-gradient(100deg,#1a55cf,#6f2ee0)]` and `text-white` land on the same element. This fixes all four call sites that had the bug: the "Selected" button and "Most popular" ribbon on `OrderBits.tsx`'s `PlanCard`, the storage quick-pick buttons, and the hosting-plan "Most popular" ribbon in `DeployView.tsx` itself (~line 1710). Two other spots (`text-[#fff]` at OrderBits.tsx:185, 236) already dodged this bug correctly.

### 2. OS grid clipping
`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`, `ImagePicker()` (~line 1111). The grid itself (`auto-fill, minmax(96px,1fr)`) can't overflow horizontally — that's not the bug. The real exposure: this Fold's height is at the mercy of `Deck`'s JS-measured slide height (`ResizeObserver` → `.deck`'s hard `overflow-hidden`, ~line 165), and the Fold's own CSS-driven expand animation can outrun that measurement, or the real catalogue (Windows/CentOS/Fedora/Arch are all already mapped in `familyLabel`) can simply carry more OS families than this sandbox's four — either way, rows get sliced off by the outer `overflow-hidden` with no scrollbar and no way to reach them. Fix: gave the family grid its own `max-h-[300px] overflow-y-auto`, so it scrolls internally regardless of how the outer deck sizes itself. The codebase's own default scrollbar styling (`app/globals.css:728-731`) makes this a visible, if you will discoverable, affordance automatically — no extra CSS needed.

### 3. Add-ons checkbox contrast
Markup is in `OrderBits.tsx`'s `AddonRow` (outside my edit scope), so fixed via `app/globals.css`. Unchecked state was `border-rim-hi bg-well` — in dark mode `bg-well` (#000c1e) is nearly identical to the card's own surface, in light mode the border measures ~1.6:1 against white (WCAG wants 3:1 for UI boundaries) — so "off" read as empty space, not a control, next to the checked state's solid gradient fill. Added a scoped override (matched on the tile's unique 19px/5px-radius combo, verified unique repo-wide) giving the unchecked box a real border and a faint blue tint in both themes.

### 4. "Recommended" badge contrast (site-wide)
Not a shared CSS class as assumed — it's a literal recipe (`border-[rgba(72,148,255,.35)] bg-[rgba(10,40,96,.5)] text-[#8dbde8]`) copy-pasted twice in `OrderBits.tsx`: `RegionCard`'s badge and `Fold`'s generic `badge` prop (used for "Recommended" on Server settings, `DeployView.tsx:1384`). Dark mode measures ~7.5:1 (fine). Light mode measures ~1.5:1 — the dark-navy wash blends toward pale blue-grey on a white card and the equally pale text nearly vanishes. Added a light-mode override in `globals.css` scoped to `text-[#8dbde8]` (confirmed the only two uses of that exact color repo-wide) giving it a dark, saturated blue ink on a light blue tint (~6.5:1). Left the visually-similar `text-[#9dbdee]` "+N add-ons" chip untouched since it wasn't part of the report.

### 5. Germany region — investigated, found no code bug
Traced the full path: DB has 3 enabled `Node` rows (`sgp1`, `ash1`, `fsn1`/Falkenstein-Germany), `lib/node-regions.ts` has real coordinates/labels for `fsn1`, and `regionsFrom()` in `lib/nx/catalog.ts` (called from `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`) does no capacity or provider filtering — I ran it directly against the current DB rows and it correctly returns all 3 regions including "Falkenstein, DE". There is no filter, active flag, or query bug excluding Germany in the current code — **Germany is already fully configured and the code path already includes it.** I could not get a live-browser reproduction to confirm what the site owner actually saw (sandboxed network blocked both the public URL and localhost). Left `lib/node-regions.ts` untouched since there's nothing to fix there. If the wizard is still only showing Singapore live, that points to a stale build/deploy or cache rather than a source bug — worth a rebuild+reload check rather than a further code change. One unrelated data-quality note: the `fsn1` and `ash1` Node rows are tagged provider `OVH` even though `lib/node-regions.ts` classifies both codes under `HETZNER` — doesn't affect the customer-facing picker, but worth the owner's attention for admin-side validation.

### 6. "First month free" on Cloud Hosting
Confirmed via `lib/promotions.ts` and `lib/promo-redemption.ts` (`FIRST_MONTH_FREE_SERVICES = ["HOSTING"]`) that this promo is real and scoped to Shared/Cloud Hosting only, and found the established site-wide convention in `components/marketing/ProductPricing.tsx` (a banner) and `components/customer/HostingDeployWizard.tsx` (per-card "Free first month" / "then $X/mo", read-only reference per your allowance). `DeployView.tsx`'s Cloud Hosting flow had neither — the service tile and the plan cards both showed plain pricing with no mention of the promo. Added: a small "First month free" pill on the Cloud Hosting service tile (~line 1350), and replaced the flat price on the hosting plan cards with the same "Free first month" / "then $X/mo" framing (~line 1741), matching `HostingDeployWizard.tsx`'s wording and using the app's `text-mint` token (theme-aware) rather than a raw un-themed color.
